stemMd: A retailer says its new website increased sales because website sales rose sharply after launch. Which information most directly bears on whether the retailer's total sales increased?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Whether the website contains a company history.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Whether website purchases replaced purchases that customers would otherwise have made in its stores.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Whether the website uses a different typeface.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Whether the launch was announced to staff.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Whether online orders are numbered sequentially.

explanationMd: Growth in one channel can reflect migration from another rather than new demand. To assess total sales, count online and store sales together and determine whether the website merely shifted existing purchases.

distractorRationale.c: Design alone does not establish net sales.
distractorRationale.d: Staff awareness does not quantify customer substitution.
distractorRationale.e: Order numbering does not compare channels.
distractorRationale.a: Informational content does not establish total purchasing.
